reviewScope: Untrusted ZIP/TAR member names, absolute/traversal paths, links/reparse points, collisions, malformed records, expansion limits, in-memory indexing, and non-extraction behavior.
JavaScript/TypeScript parser resource bounds, malformed syntax, TypeScript 5.9.3 runtime dependency, and clean-room execution.

MCP principal and session binding, single-principal mode, token workspace override, workspace boundary, approval levels, report/task access, and output redaction tests.

limitations: This is not an independent audit, penetration test, legal opinion, or human certification.
No hostile external binary was submitted to Ghidra; Ghidra is a native parser and is not sandboxed by ArmorBreak.
Only one Windows OS principal was available for the package drill. Cross-account isolation is outside the declared single-principal product scope and remains unverified.

The npm lockfile resolves TypeScript through registry.npmmirror.com with a pinned integrity value; the clean-room command requested registry.npmjs.org. The source discrepancy is disclosed in the package/license inventory.
No final exact-main build, production OIDC attestation, Tag workflow, or public Release exists in this report.

observations: ZIP/TAR entries are indexed in memory and not extracted by artifact intake.
Tests cover absolute and parent paths, backslash traversal, ADS/device names, links/reparse points, collisions, zip bombs, malformed records, and TAR metadata/link rejection.
coverage.remaining: No independent archive fuzzing or external hostile corpus was run.

observations: Uses the pinned TypeScript Compiler API; AST depth is capped at 256 and nodes at 50,000 per file.
Over-budget inputs produce PARTIAL results and warnings; no emit, tsconfig loading, cross-file resolution, data flow, or target execution is claimed.
Actual clean-room archive parsed one JavaScript and one TypeScript input and returned both task/report records.
coverage.remaining: No large-scale parser fuzzing; semantics and cross-file resolution are unsupported.

observations: Ghidra 12.1.4/JDK 21 are resolved from configured/trusted host locations; target bytes originate from Core authorization and are copied to a fixed input.bin path.
Arguments use execFile without shell expansion; timeout is capped at 600 seconds and captured output at 32 MiB; the report is bounded and temp directories are removed in finally.
coverage.remaining: Native Ghidra remains attackable by hostile samples; no sandbox/hostile-sample containment is claimed. Use only authorized data and hosts.

observations: Evidence and audit serializers call redactText/redactDeep; tests cover credential-like values, secrets, and bounded excerpts.
Portable evidence path fields now use archive basenames rather than machine absolute paths.
coverage.remaining: No exhaustive manual review of every third-party tool output and every serializer was performed.

observations: HTTP mode rejects multiple principals and workspace overrides; sessions bind to the configured identity.

The Windows package drill verified current-user ACLs, denied broad built-in principals, rejected out-of-workspace targets, checked host config, and denied a foreign CLI task/report to a separate MCP session.
coverage.remaining: Two distinct Windows accounts and cross-account private evidence access were not tested; shared/multi-user service is unsupported.

findings.title: Ghidra is not a hostile-input sandbox
findings.disposition: Ghidra is separate L1, requires per-task authorization, uses bounded process/output settings and an exact temporary copy. The product will not claim safe sandboxing of hostile binaries.
findings.retest: Exact-main full CI, tests, and V2.2-to-V2.3.1 Windows drill passed in run 42454358071. The drill exercised the authorized host approval path, but no hostile Ghidra corpus or OS-level containment proof was run; Ghidra remains an unsandboxed external process.

findings.title: No two-account Windows isolation result
findings.disposition: V2.3 HTTP service is explicitly single-principal and rejects multi-principal configuration. Cross-account service mode is outside supported scope; no two-account test is claimed.
findings.retest: Run 42454358071 verified current-user ACL, principal binding, MCP session separation, workspace boundary, and rollback hashes under one Windows SID. A genuinely separate second Windows account was unavailable and remains unverified.

findings.title: Behavior comparison depends on caller-supplied observations
findings.disposition: No execution or global equivalence claim is made; the contract labels unverified caller provenance.
findings.retest: Exact-main tests passed, but the comparator still consumes finite caller-supplied observations and does not authenticate their external origin.
